extraction.name: MINT-1T
extraction.description: An open-source multimodal interleaved pre-training dataset containing approximately 1.02 trillion text tokens, 3.42 billion images, and 1054.3 million documents: 1029.4 million HTML documents, 24.0 million PDF documents, and 0.87 million ArXiv documents. Each document contains interleaved text and image references. Released HTML instances contain text and image URLs; PDF and ArXiv instances contain text, document URLs, and image reference numbers.
extraction.creator: A team from the University of Washington, Salesforce Research, Stanford University, University of Texas at Austin, and University of California, Berkeley.
extraction.citeAs: Anas Awadalla, Le Xue, Oscar Lo, Manli Shu, Hannah Lee, Etash Guha, Matt Jordan, Sheng Shen, Mohamed Awadalla, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Ran Xu, Yejin Choi, and Ludwig Schmidt. MINT-1T: Scaling Open-Source Multimodal Data by 10x: A Multimodal Dataset with One Trillion Tokens. arXiv:2406.11271v5, 31 October 2024. Preprint, under review.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors collected and parsed multimodal documents from CommonCrawl HTML and PDF dumps and ArXiv S3 buckets. HTML interleaved sequences were extracted by parsing DOM trees in CommonCrawl WARC entries. PDF links were extracted from CommonCrawl WAT files, downloaded, and parsed with PyMuPDF; text blocks were ordered by column and position, and images were interleaved according to proximity to text blocks. ArXiv documents were constructed from LaTeX source using TexSoup to locate figures and interleave images with text. Quality filtering and deduplication methods were validated by training multiple large multimodal models. Only the authors participated in collection; no crowdworkers or contractors were involved.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The datasheet reports no missing information in individual instances. During collection, non-retrievable image links were discarded and documents without valid image links were removed. The released dataset relies on external URLs whose continued availability is not guaranteed because of link rot. PDF parsing sometimes fails to detect images.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Public-web HTML documents from CommonCrawl WARC dumps, PDF documents linked in CommonCrawl WAT dumps, and ArXiv LaTeX source documents obtained directly from ArXiv S3 buckets. HTML sources cover May 2017 through April 2024, using full dumps from October 2018 onward and partial earlier dumps; PDF sources cover February 2023 through April 2024. Raw data are not provided because they may contain offensive content.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: January 2024 to June 2024. The datasheet states that the underlying web data span 2013 to 2024.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Email addresses were replaced with templates such as email@example.com, and IP addresses were replaced with randomly generated non-functional IPs. For multi-file ArXiv papers, input tags in the main TeX file were replaced with the referenced files' contents; imports, bibliography, tables, and citation tags were removed. PDF reading order was reconstructed by clustering text blocks into columns and ordering them from top left to bottom right, with images anchored according to bounding-box proximity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: HTML documents with no images, more than 30 images, or image URLs containing inappropriate substrings were removed. PDFs larger than 50 MB or longer than 50 pages were discarded, and pages without text were excluded. Non-English documents were removed using FastText language identification with a confidence threshold of 0.65. URL-based NSFW filtering, RefinedWeb duplicate n-gram filters, and MassiveText quality rules removed undesirable or low-quality text. Images smaller than 150 pixels or larger than 20,000 pixels were removed; maximum aspect ratios were two for HTML and three for PDFs. Documents containing an NSFW image were discarded. Text deduplication used a Bloom filter with a 0.01 false-positive rate and 13-gram paragraph matching; documents with more than 80% duplicate paragraphs were discarded. Exact paragraph deduplication on 2% of each CommonCrawl snapshot removed common HTML boilerplate. SHA256-based image filtering removed images occurring more than ten times per snapshot; repeated images within a document were reduced to their first occurrence. Deduplication was performed separately for each source. The ArXiv pipeline did not apply the subsequent filtering and deduplication described for CommonCrawl sources.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The datasheet states that labels or targets associated with individual instances are not applicable. For a separate domain-composition analysis, an LDA model produced 200 topics from sampled documents, and GPT-4 classified topic word sets into dominant domains based on MMMU domains.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: FastText language identification model for language filtering; GantMan/nsfw_model for NSFW image detection; GPT-4 for classifying LDA topic word sets into domains in the separate dataset-composition analysis.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors will maintain the dataset, respond to issues, and update it. Updates and an erratum will be communicated through the Hugging Face dataset README; no update frequency is specified. Owners can be contacted by email or through Hugging Face Issues. Older versions will remain accessible through repository Git history, with their issues documented in the erratum. Contributions will be accepted through Hugging Face pull requests. A Google form will be provided to request removal of samples.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset may contain images of individuals, text about specific individuals, confidential content, and sensitive personal data if such information is present on the public web. The authors do not explicitly identify subpopulations, although subpopulation information may be extractable. Email addresses and IP addresses are masked, but direct or indirect identification of individuals remains possible.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: MINT-1T is intended to make large multimodal model research and open science more accessible by addressing the shortage of large-scale open-source interleaved training data. The authors acknowledge risks from exposing harmful web content and leaking personal data, despite PII masking and NSFW filtering. Individuals were not explicitly notified of collection, and no ethical review or data-subject impact analysis was conducted. The paper states that CommonCrawl respects robots.txt and promises a sample-removal form. Further work is recommended to improve the safety of multimodal internet data.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The HTML subset is described as not strongly biased toward a specific domain. The PDF subset has a higher proportion of Science and Technology documents, attributed to the use of PDFs for scientific and technical communication. Non-English documents are filtered out. The authors avoid text-quality classifier models because previous work has shown that they favor text from certain demographics, and encourage consumers to further filter the dataset for their use case.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: PyMuPDF sometimes fails to detect images and can extract incorrect reading order from arbitrary PDF layouts, including reading across column boundaries or starting with the rightmost column. The dataset is not self-contained: users must retrieve external images, and URL availability is not guaranteed. Hosting the complete dataset with images is considered infeasible because it exceeds 300 TB. Offensive, confidential, sensitive, or identifying content may remain despite filtering. Training models that ingest or generate personally identifying information, including faces and other sensitive content, and military applications are explicitly inappropriate uses. The dataset is primarily a research artifact; users must independently verify legal compliance for commercial use.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Pre-training large multimodal models that process multiple interleaved images and text. The dataset has been used to train models and compare data quality against competing datasets. Additional proposed uses include generating interleaved image-text sequences and building multimodal document retrieval systems. Only a training split is provided. Consumers are encouraged to apply additional use-case-specific filtering. Uses involving personally identifying information or military applications are inappropriate, and commercial users are responsible for verifying legal compliance.
